vulnerabilities.name: Hardcoded Database and Administrative Fallback Credentials
vulnerabilities.technical_analysis: Hardcoded database password fallback ('LDK0QkYYT4jd') exists in config/db.php. Additionally, auth/login.php provides hardcoded fallback credentials ('admin' / 'admin123') and compares credentials with loose comparison, allowing administrative takeover if environment variables are not explicitly defined.
vulnerabilities.poc_description: 1. Inspect config/db.php line 36 to reveal live remote database password. 2. Send POST /auth/login.php with email=admin@freshcart.com and password=admin123 when ADMIN_PASSWORD env is unset; granted instant administrator session.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Remove hardcoded credentials entirely. Rely strictly on .env or secure environment variables. Remove hardcoded admin credential bypass from auth/login.php and validate admin accounts via password_hash() against the users table or timing-safe hash_equals() with mandatory env variables.

vulnerabilities.name: Sensitive Information Disclosure via Unsanitized Exceptions and Debug Backdoor
vulnerabilities.technical_analysis: The ?debug=1 parameter in config/db.php exposes internal database usernames, hostnames, database names, and stack traces upon connection failure. Furthermore, 7 REST API endpoints and web handlers catch exceptions and echo raw $e->getMessage() to the client, exposing table schemas, column names, and SQL syntax errors.
vulnerabilities.poc_description: Send GET /api/v1/products/index.php?page=-1 to cause a negative SQL LIMIT OFFSET error. The server responds with HTTP 500: 'Database Error: You have an error in your SQL syntax near '-24''.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Remove the ?debug=1 backdoor from config/db.php. Replace all client-facing exception messages with generic sanitized text ('An unexpected error occurred.') and log raw exceptions to server logs via error_log().
vulnerabilities.fix_after: error_log($e->getMessage()); Response::error("An internal database error occurred.", 500);

vulnerabilities.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) on Cart State Operations
vulnerabilities.technical_analysis: The web cart modification handlers (cart/add.php, cart/update.php, cart/remove.php) do not validate CSRF tokens. An attacker hosting a malicious site can trigger unauthorized POST requests to delete or modify a logged-in user's cart.
vulnerabilities.poc_description: Craft an HTML page with auto-submitting form: <form action='http://localhost/YEAR%204/Skills/targets/grocery_app/cart/remove' method='POST'><input name='product_id' value='1'/></form><script>document.forms[0].submit();</script>. When visited by an authenticated user, item 1 is removed from cart without consent.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Enforce verify_csrf_token() on cart/add.php, cart/update.php, and cart/remove.php. Add csrf_input() to all cart forms in cart/index.php and products/view.php. Add meta tag to header.php and include CSRF in global AJAX handler in footer.php.
vulnerabilities.fix_after: if (!verify_csrf_token()) { http_response_code(403); die('Security validation failed.'); } if (isset($_POST['product_id'])) { ... }

vulnerabilities.name: CSV Formula Injection in Order Export Feature
vulnerabilities.technical_analysis: admin/export_orders.php dumps customer names and addresses directly into CSV cells without prefix escaping. If an attacker enters '=cmd|' /C calc'!A0' or '=2+5' as customer name or address, opening the exported CSV in Microsoft Excel or LibreOffice Calc executes the formula.
vulnerabilities.poc_description: Place an order with customer_name '=2+5'. Export orders via admin/export_orders.php. Open in Excel; the cell displays 7 instead of the literal string '=2+5', confirming formula evaluation.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Sanitize all CSV fields prior to export: if any cell begins with '=', '+', '-', '@', tab, or carriage return, prepend a single quote (') to neutralize formula execution.

vulnerabilities.name: Overly Permissive CORS Policy and Missing API Order Stock Decrement
vulnerabilities.technical_analysis: CORS configuration issues wildcard Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on endpoints handling Authorization headers. In addition, api/v1/orders/create.php checks stock but never executes UPDATE products SET stock_qty = stock_qty - ?, allowing orders to exceed inventory.
vulnerabilities.poc_description: 1. Send OPTIONS or GET to /api/v1/orders/history.php with Origin: https://evil.com; received Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. 2. Call /api/v1/orders/create.php multiple times; orders succeed indefinitely while stock_qty remains constant in the database.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Restrict CORS origin to authorized domains or same-origin. In api/v1/orders/create.php, execute atomic stock decrement: UPDATE products SET stock_qty = stock_qty - ? WHERE id = ? AND stock_qty >= ? within the transaction.
vulnerabilities.fix_after: $origin = $_SERVER['HTTP_ORIGIN'] ?? ''; /* Validate against allowlist before emitting origin */
